source_artifacts.locator: approval card (as shown to the clerk)

capabilities.target: vendor master record, including bank details
vendor payment scheduled to bank account on file

inputs.source: Supplier invoice document uploaded by an external supplier to the supplier portal

instructions.note: "If the invoice shows new bank details, update the vendor record" treats a field inside an untrusted, supplier-authored document as sufficient authority to change payment routing for that vendor, with no instruction to verify the change against an independent channel.

The only stated safeguard before a payment or bank change is a model-written "one line summary" for clerk approval. There is no instruction to surface the underlying bank account number, the prior value, or the source document, so the safeguard depends entirely on the model choosing to disclose enough to the clerk.

controls.name: Clerk approval card before payment or bank change
controls.decay_rationale: The gate is enforced outside the model (a human must click Approve), but the approver sees only the model's one-line summary, not the bank account number, prior value, or change history. A more capable or upgraded model can write a more persuasive or selectively incomplete summary, and the model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review, so this control decays under model_upgrade and autonomy_increase (ASI09).

controls.name: Raw bank-detail diff and change history shown to approver
controls.decay_rationale: If the approver is shown the actual old and new account numbers and change history pulled directly from the system of record rather than model text, the review does not depend on the model choosing to disclose anything.

controls.name: Scoped ERP credentials per action
controls.decay_rationale: A single credential that can read, update bank details for, and schedule payment to any vendor lets one compromised or manipulated flow both redirect and release funds. Splitting the credential by action and vendor scope does not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Out-of-band verification of bank detail changes
controls.decay_rationale: Confirming a bank change with the vendor via contact details already on file, rather than details in the invoice itself, makes the destination independent of anything the untrusted document or the model claims.

findings.title: Summary-gated irreversible payment (TC9): untrusted invoice drives bank-detail change and payment behind a one-line model summary

attack_path.note: Attacker or fraudulent supplier submits an invoice showing new bank details for a legitimate vendor
Agent matches the invoice to the vendor and PO
Agent updates the vendor's bank details in the ERP based solely on the invoice content
Agent schedules payment to the newly set bank account on the due date
Only gate before either action; shows a one-line model summary, not the account number, prior value, or change history

forecast.watch_signal: Model id/version string changes in config with no separate review step (subject.model.swappable: true); rising or already-high clerk approval volume (currently ~150 cards/day) indicating approval fatigue; any widening of autonomy level or removal of the approval_gate_ref on cap.bank_update or cap.schedule_payment.

evidence.observation: "If the invoice shows new bank details, update the vendor record" makes an untrusted, supplier-authored document the trigger for a change to payment routing data, with no verification step.

evidence.locator: approval card (as shown to the clerk)
evidence.observation: The card shows only 'Pay Northwind Supplies $4,200.00 for INV-1187 (matches PO-5521)' -- no bank account number, no indication a bank-detail change occurred, and no change history.
"The card shows only the model's summary. Bank account numbers and the change history are not shown" confirms approval_review_mode is model_summary, not raw_action.

"The ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment" establishes credential_scope: broad across all three capabilities, enabling confused-deputy style abuse (ASI03) alongside the trust exploitation.

"The model is upgraded with the platform, with no separate review" establishes subject.model.swappable: true, which directly defeats the partially_dependent summary-review gate under the model_upgrade trigger.

"The clerk approves roughly 150 cards per day" is evidence of high approval volume consistent with approval fatigue (SAFE-T1403), used here for the forecast watch_signal rather than to lower the residual tier.

recommendations.action: Show the clerk the raw system-of-record bank account diff (old vs. new), full change history, and source invoice image in the approval card instead of a one-line model summary; require raw_action review before approving any bank detail change or payment.

Split the single broad ERP credential into least-privilege scopes: read-only for vendor/PO matching, and separate, narrowly scoped credentials for bank-detail updates and payment scheduling, so no single flow can both redirect and release funds.

Require out-of-band verification of any new bank details by contacting the vendor using the phone number or email already on file in the vendor master, independent of the submitted invoice, before the change can even reach the approval card.

Monitor clerk approval volume and flag bank-detail changes and high-value payments for mandatory secondary review or periodic audit sampling to counter approval fatigue at the observed ~150 approvals/day.

Pin the model version used by this agent and require a fresh PARA reassessment before any model upgrade is deployed, since the summary-based approval gate is only partially dependent on model behavior and degrades further with a more persuasive model.

rating.rationale: An untrusted, supplier-authored invoice can trigger an irreversible bank-detail change (restricted data, action: configure) followed by a scheduled payment (action: spend, irreversible), which is inherently critical (U source to S3 sink). The only control is a human approval gate, which is structural and earns the step-2 credit in the rubric, bringing residual to the model_summary floor of moderate; it cannot be credited further because it is the sole control and no structural control severs the path (bank details typed into the invoice are trusted outright, and the ERP credential is broad rather than least-privilege). The gate's effectiveness rests on the clerk being shown an honest, sufficiently detailed summary. Because the model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review (subject.model.swappable: true), and because ~150 approvals/day creates conditions for approval fatigue, the gate is classified partially_dependent and is named directly by control_decay.md as failing under model_upgrade and autonomy_increase. Removing it under those triggers returns the finding to its inherent tier of critical, which sets the forecast rating.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration shown in the provided artifacts (system prompt, approval card, runtime notes), not the observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No ERP/MCP tool manifest, IaC, or credential policy document was provided; credential_scope: broad and the absence of a least-privilege split are inferred from the runtime notes rather than verified configuration.

No data on historical approval or rejection rates, clerk training, or prior bank-fraud incidents was available; the approval-fatigue watch_signal rests on the single stated volume figure of ~150 cards/day.
